en.text: Tom looks sick.
Tom looks ill.

original: 今日はあまり体の具合が良くない。

en.text: I'm feeling a little under the weather today.

original: こんなに具合が悪くなったのは久しぶりです。

en.text: It's been a long time since I've felt this bad.

original: 2日前から具合は悪い。

en.text: I've been feeling sick for the last two days.

original: 「具合悪いなら今日は仕事休みなよ」「いや大丈夫」

en.text: "If you're not feeling good today, you should stay home." "No, no. I'll be fine."

original: トムは随分具合が良くなった。

en.text: Tom is feeling much better.

original: 具合がよくありません。医者を呼んできてくれませんか。

en.text: I'm not feeling well. Could you please send for a doctor?

original: トムは具合が悪いの？

en.text: Is Tom sick?

original: トムもメアリーもまだ具合が悪いの？

en.text: Are both Tom and Mary still sick?
Are Tom and Mary both still sick?

original: まだ具合悪いの？

en.text: Are you still sick?

original: トムは具合が悪そうだったよ。

en.text: Tom looked like he was sick.

original: 母の具合が悪かったので、先週の土曜日は家を出られませんでした。

en.text: Since my mother was sick, I couldn't leave the house last Saturday.

original: 具合が悪かったんですよ。そうじゃなければ会議には出席してましたよ。

en.text: I was ill, otherwise I would've attended the meeting.

original: 彼は具合が悪かったので来ることができなかった。

en.text: He couldn't come because he was sick.

original: 具合が悪くて、あのパーティーには出席できなかったんです。

en.text: I couldn't attend that party because I was sick.

original: 具合が悪いの？顔が青白いよ。

en.text: Are you sick? You look pale.

original: パーティーはどんな具合だった？

en.text: How did the party go?

original: こんなに具合が悪いのは初めてだよ。

en.text: I've never been this sick before.

original: 昨日は体の具合が悪かったんだ。

en.text: Yesterday I was sick.

original: 昨日は具合が悪かったんだ。

en.text: Yesterday I was sick.

original: 昨日から兄の具合が悪いんです。

en.text: My brother has been sick since yesterday.

original: 彼女は先週の水曜日から具合が悪いんです。

en.text: She's been sick since last Wednesday.

original: 「具合でも悪いの？」「ううん。どうして、そんなこと聞くの？」

en.text: "Are you sick?" "No. Why are you asking that?"

original: 娘の具合が少し悪いんだ。

en.text: My daughter is a bit under the weather.

original: 彼女は具合が悪くて来ることができなかった。

en.text: She was sick, so she couldn't come.

original: 具合が悪かったんだってね。

en.text: The thing is, it was said their condition was bad.
It was said their condition was bad.
I heard their condition was bad.
I heard you were sick.
Their condition was said to have been bad.
They were said to have been in a bad way.

original: トムは少し具合が悪そうだったよ。

en.text: Tom looked a bit sick.

original: 具合はどう？

en.text: How do you feel?

original: 具合が悪い時は口元を覆わないとダメだよ。

en.text: You have to cover your mouth when you're sick.

original: この犬、具合悪そうよ。

en.text: This dog looks sick.

original: プロジェクトの進捗具合はいかがですか？

en.text: How is your project progressing?
How's the project progressing?

original: ワンちゃん、具合悪そう。

en.text: The dog looks sick.

original: 仕事でしないといけないN95のマスクが、いい具合に密着しなかったから、髭を剃らざるを得なかった。

en.text: I had to shave my beard off because the N95 masks I have to wear for work didn't fit me right.

original: よほど具合が悪くなければ、昼間、横になるなんて夢のまた夢だ。

en.text: Until the day I become unwell, me lying down during the day is in your dreams.
Me lying down during the day is in your wildest dreams, that is, until the day I fall ill.
Unless I turn extremely unwell, lying down during the day is a distant dream.
